title: Combined-hardening material path and global cyclic lifecycle
purpose: Verify AgentFEM's small-strain combined-hardening implementation against the published Abaqus model definition and parameter style, then exercise its native global quadrature, reversal, result, rollback and restart lifecycle.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain J2 plasticity with exponential isotropic and multi-component Armstrong--Frederick kinematic hardening

source.title: Models for metals subjected to cyclic loading
source.case: Combined nonlinear isotropic/kinematic hardening equations and published-style parameterization

execution.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_constitutive_models.py -k chaboche && python -m pytest -q tests/test_p1_platform.py -k global_chaboche_cycle
execution.evidence: Material-point tests enforce the shifted yield surface, discrete tangent and reversal; the global unit-cube cycle enforces quadrature-state use, standard fields and checkpoint/restart equivalence.

observables: Shifted Mises stress and current isotropic yield radius after return mapping.
Multi-component backstress and Bauschinger reversal response.
Directional derivative of the fully discrete stress update.
Global S, PE, PEEQ, ALPHA and MISES fields plus restarted final state.
acceptance: The converged material point lies on the current shifted yield surface.
The algorithmic tensor reproduces an independent directional finite difference of the discrete map.
A reversed path advances PEEQ and reverses the axial backstress direction.
Interrupted and uninterrupted global paths recover the same displacement and backstress fields.
limitations: This evidence checks the published constitutive definition and AgentFEM lifecycle; it does not reproduce a proprietary or experimental stabilized hysteresis curve.
Structure-level cyclic calibration and complete recovery-dissipation energy closure remain promotion gates.
